result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers find the same core problems and give concrete fixes. B explains more clearly that the links aren't tied to any sentence, and it separates what the company controls from what the bank controls, which shows which parts of the answer are firm and which are guesses. B also ranks its changes by severity. A is strong and slightly more practical on feedback metrics, but it ties sources to claims less directly. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers cover the same ground with concrete fixes, including a path to a person and a thumbs-down that asks what went wrong. Answer A says outright that the links aren't tied to any sentence, so customers can't check the 30-day rule, and it points out that the bot is guessing because it doesn't know the purchase date. A also ranks each change by severity. Answer B is just as concrete but less explicit about the link-to-claim gap, and its prioritisation is looser: it ends on reordering the links.
